slides.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE HAZARD A GUESS To have a guess about someone or something He always hazards guesses, so be careful. GRASP AT A STRAW To be unsure about something and still state an opinion I think he is just grasping at a straw. READ SOMEONE’S MIND To deduce what someone else is thinking She will never call; It’s like I read her mind. A SHOT IN THE DARK To venture guessing something you are not certain about John accused Oliver, he just took a shot in the dark. ANYONE’S GUESS A mystery or something unpredictable It's anyone's guess what his next book will be about. TAKE A STAB AT To give it a try or a shot Mary went for it and took a stab at the application. SEAT-OF-THE-PANTS To describe something improvised or done based on prior experience Why are you doing this by seat-of-the-pants? BARK UP THE WRONG TREE To be wrong about something or someone; To be wrong about the reasons or ways to achieve something Stop accusing me lady, you’re barking up the wrong tree,

Language bricks

slides.title: We are able to express ideas about things or event likely to happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.
visibleTexts: We are able to express ideas about things or event likely to happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.

PHRASES EXAMPLES What if… John, we should call Tim, what if he takes a stab at the meeting and all goes wrong? Imagine that / if… Imagine if Mary shows up at the wedding, we need to warn them. In case… We should phone them in case they are lost; don’t you think? Suppose / Supposing that Delia is talking to Jim in advance, supposing that he wants to come and make a scene To Consider 1. We work with these phrases using the simple present tense. 2. When using what if we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 3. The context will determine if the situation likely to happen is in the present or future. 4. Modals can help out build a context.

Functional English

slides.title: Functions Examples Express ideas or events likely to be true or to happen I need to let Sean know in case he expects her to be here. We need to leave this place; what if they come back? Imagine that Shane shows up; what do we tell Jake? Suppose that Mike can make it, does it mean we seal the deal?

C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher.

Possible Potential Outcomes from COVID-19 Complications on Testes: Lesson from SARS Infection Coronavirus infection disease-2019 (COVID-19) gained worldwide fame after deadly outbreak in China and its subsequent spread to many countries. So far, COVID-19 is not fully contained, and new cases are arising on daily bases in various countries, Imagine if it keeps growing. Due to zoonotic nature and human-to-human spread, COVID-19 is considered pandemic with more causalities in developing countries. Full genome analysis revealed its resemblance with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) virus with minor variation in non-structural proteins. Both viruses use the common angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE2) receptor to attach to the epithelial cells of the target organs. Currently, in case someone gets COVID-19, those patients are treated with drugs that are used for lungs infections. However, ACE2 has high expression in other human organs such as kidney and testes. So what if that’s not enough? Thus, it is assumed that, like SARS, it may have adverse effects on other vital organs, which have dominant expression of ACE2. In testis, SARS affected patients displayed peritubular fibrosis, extensive germ cell disruption, damage of blood-testis barrier integrity and more frequent occurrence of apoptosis. Here, we critically discuss the possible adverse effects of COVID-19 on the testes of patients along with future precautions to overcome the complications of reproductive organs. Adapted from: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33115584/
